proposition: For the PG owner, RentOK is the cheat code: the five things that stop him every month stop being obstacles and become ground he runs over.

board.style_line: Original side-scrolling video-game world built for this film alone, flat 2-D staging in exactly three tonal planes - unpainted grey cement render above, slate overcast sky behind, one matte cobalt-blue #0038FF floor band across the bottom fifth of the frame - one light direction from upper frame-left, sparse frame with no props, no crowds, no particles and no background city; a photographically real man rendered into the flat world; 9:16 vertical, 30fps, no reference to any existing game, franchise, character, mascot or artwork.
board.negative_line: no text, no lettering, no numerals, no captions, no subtitles, no signage, no shop boards, no nameplates, no user-interface copy, no app screens with writing, no logos, no watermarks, no brand marks of any kind, no Mario, no plumber, no red cap or dungarees, no mushrooms, no coins, no question blocks, no turtles, no pixel-font glyphs, no Japanese game assets, no firearms, no muzzle flash, no explosions, no blood, no celebrity or public-figure likeness, no children, no religious imagery, no national symbols, no Devanagari or any non-Latin script.

identity_anchors.owner: A 52-year-old Indian man, medium-brown skin, stocky build, upright posture, close-cropped grey-flecked hair, thick moustache, rimless glasses, a short-sleeved pale-olive bush shirt tucked into dark grey trousers, brown leather chappals, a faded maroon cloth sling bag over his right shoulder with the corner of a hardbound paper register showing out of it; his face and hands keep photographic detail and weight while the world around him stays flat.
identity_anchors.phone: A plain black 6.1-inch smartphone with a single hairline crack running across the top-right corner of the screen, carried in his right hand, screen facing away from camera unless the beat states otherwise.
identity_anchors.building: A four-storey run-down paying-guest building in unpainted grey cement render, eight identical windows per floor behind dark green metal grille shutters, a black plastic water tank on a welded steel frame on the roof, a bunch of exposed black cables running down the left edge of the facade; no boards, no signs, no writing anywhere on it.
identity_anchors.floor_band: A perfectly level matte cobalt-blue band of colour #0038FF occupying the bottom fifth of the frame, no texture, no pattern, no reflection, carrying no shadow except the man's own.
identity_anchors.obstacle_slab: A blank grey concrete slab one and a half times the man's height, square-topped, rising vertically out of the cobalt floor band, its face completely smooth and unmarked.

hero_frame.description: The owner standing on the roof of his own building, one hand resting on the steel frame of his water tank, stopped and turned to look back down the way he came; in the same vertical frame, below and behind him, the whole run of the level lies cleared - five grey slabs flat in the floor, the pit closed into unbroken cobalt, the falling debris settled - and the phone hangs low in his other hand, throwing cyan up onto his forearm and the underside of his jaw as the only saturated colour and the only light on his face. No text anywhere in the frame.

audio.music_bed: Composed to picture, no voice of any kind. Phone buzz and dry room tone under the first frame, committing to the game register from the opening second rather than switching into it later. A dull, deliberately off-tune two-note stall on each impact, at the same level each time, reading as the word no. Complete silence for 0.8 s at the cheat code. One rising synth tone enters with the cyan outline and carries unbroken through the five clears, resolving on the roof and stopping one second before the hero frame ends, leaving clean rooftop ambience under it. A single hard cut of silence into the close card. The whole film is designed to lose nothing that carries the sale when it is played muted.

beats.title: Eleven at night, still working
beats.feeling: The private, unglamorous tiredness of a man still at work at an hour when the work should be over - recognition arriving before sympathy does.
beats.framing: Extreme close-up: the man's right thumb at the exact centre of frame on the cracked phone screen, the screen the only light source, a column of unread grey message bubbles stacking upward faster than the thumb can move; the rest of the frame is unresolved dark. From 0.7 s the camera dollies straight back along the lens axis, no pan and no tilt, for 1.4 s, and the same man is revealed in full figure standing at the left third of the vertical frame on the flat cobalt floor band, his four-storey building rising behind him into the top two-thirds, every window lit. Five small grey key glyphs sit in the top-left corner. On the last beat he starts to run to frame right.
beats.first_frame: Only the thumb, the cracked screen and the stack of grey message bubbles, lit by the screen alone against unresolved dark. Nothing yet says game and nothing yet says advertisement.
beats.impact: One move, on one axis, with no cut inside the beat: the surprise is not a cut but the reveal that a photographically real man is standing in a flat 2-D level. The pull-back carries two lightings - screen-only at the tight end, overcast key from upper frame-left at the wide end - which is the reason the beat is a dolly and not a zoom. Sound is phone buzz and room tone only, no music, committing to the register the film keeps. The beat leaves on his second stride landing on the cobalt band, which is the motivation out.

beats.title: Two walls in nine strides
beats.feeling: The flat, familiar irritation of being stopped by something you already knew was coming - not shock, the fourth time this month.
beats.framing: Continuous left-to-right lateral track at his running speed, the building sliding past behind him. A blank grey slab rises out of the cobalt floor at the right edge and reaches full height as he arrives; TENANT VERIFICATION composites on its smooth face in the upper third. He hits it chest-first and is stopped dead while the camera carries a beat past him. A second identical slab rises immediately behind the first as he steps round; COLLECTING RENT composites on it in the same screen position. Two of the five key glyphs go dark. He is still moving right.
beats.first_frame: The man mid-stride in the lower left third, the first slab exactly half-risen out of the cobalt band at the right edge of frame, its face still completely blank.
beats.impact: One attention cue for the whole beat - the arriving slab - with no camera move beyond the constant lateral track, so the eye stays on the collision rather than on the method. He is stopped, never clumsy: no stumble, no pratfall, no comic recoil. Both impacts take the same dull two-note stall at the same level, so the second lands as repetition rather than escalation. The beat leaves on the second slab's shadow crossing his face.

beats.title: The floor opens
beats.feeling: The drop in the stomach when the ground itself turns out to be the problem - the moment a bad month becomes a question about the business.
beats.framing: Same lateral track, same direction, same speed. A young tenant with a rolled mattress under one arm sprints past him from behind and out of frame right; the owner's hand comes up and closes on nothing. LEFT WITHOUT PAYING composites in the upper third where the slab labels sat. The cobalt floor ahead of him folds open into a pit filled with loose paper slips lifting in the draught; NO RECONCILIATION composites. He plants both feet at the lip. Cement chips begin raining from his own upper windows into the frame; COMPLAINTS composites. Two more key glyphs go dark, leaving one lit.
beats.first_frame: The tenant sprite already three-quarters out of frame right with the mattress, the owner's open hand still in the air where the sprite was, and the cobalt floor between them still unbroken.
beats.impact: Three events but no cut and no new location - the beat holds the one continuous scene and lets the events arrive into it, which is why it does not read as a parade. Every one of the three is a thing that happens TO him: the tenant leaves, the floor opens, the building sheds on him. The camera does not move to the pit; the pit arrives. Labels appear one at a time, never two together. The beat leaves on the last chip landing at his feet and the fourth key going dark.

beats.title: The code
beats.feeling: Held breath. Something is being entered and we have not been told what it does.
beats.framing: The lateral track stops for the first and only time. Medium shot, the man at the centre-right zone, three-quarters back to camera at the lip of the pit, feet together; he takes the phone out of the sling bag with his left hand and enters something with his right thumb. Cut to the one non-lateral framing in the film: the cracked screen filling the entire 9:16 frame, cyan #03FFF1 flooding it edge to edge, the supplied RentOK wordmark placed unaltered at its centre - the first saturated colour anywhere in the film. INSTALL composites in the upper third at 9.0 s, RENTOK APP directly beneath it at 9.4 s, both over the cyan field. No power lands yet.
beats.first_frame: The man stopped absolutely dead at the lip of the pit, phone just clearing the mouth of the bag, the rest of the frame exactly as grey as the three beats before it.
beats.impact: The only full stop in the run and the only cut in the film that changes axis - planarity and three-dimensional continuity are the criteria deliberately sacrificed here, emotion and story kept, and nothing lower is traded for them. Sound drops to complete silence for 0.8 s before the screen fills, so the cut is heard as much as seen. The gap opened in beat one is named here and left open: we have the code and not yet its effect. The wordmark and both strings are code-composited plates; the prompt for this frame specifies a blank dark screen and quotes no words.

beats.title: Immunity
beats.feeling: The lift of a weight you had stopped noticing you were carrying - relief arriving as speed, not as a smile.
beats.framing: Back on the lateral track, same direction, same speed, same distance. A thin cyan #03FFF1 outline snaps onto his silhouette in a single frame and stays; a cyan wake trails on the cobalt floor behind him. He does not slow at the pit - its two halves fold shut into unbroken cobalt under his leading foot and he runs across. The first grey slab ahead lies flat into the floor as he reaches it and becomes floor; its TENANT VERIFICATION label drops away with it and the tick DIGITAL KYC composites in cyan in the lower third. The second slab goes flat the same way and AUTOPAY composites beneath it. Two dark key glyphs relight.
beats.first_frame: The man mid-stride with the cyan outline already hard on him and nothing else in the frame changed - the same grey render, the same slate sky, the two slabs still standing ahead.
beats.impact: One cue for the beat and it is colour, not a move: the hue was set on the product in close-up in the previous beat, so it now identifies him instantly at any size on a phone, with no slow dawning. Nothing is destroyed and there is no weapon in frame; the obstacles lie down and become ground. No speed ramp, no whip pan, no lens change - the beat has to read as the same run with the resistance removed. The rising tone enters here, channelling relief the picture has already made rather than supplying it.

beats.title: Three more go flat
beats.feeling: The particular satisfaction of a run that is going right - not triumph yet, momentum.
beats.framing: Same track, unchanged. The third slab flattens into the floor ahead of him and DUES TRACKED LIVE composites in the lower third. The loose paper slips still hanging in the air from the pit gather flat into one cyan-edged plane that lays itself into the floor as he crosses it, and ONE DASHBOARD composites. The cement chips still falling from the upper windows stop dead in the air beside him, turn cyan at the edge and drop harmlessly behind him, and COMPLAINT TICKETS composites. The last two key glyphs relight, back to five.
beats.first_frame: The third slab already half sunk into the cobalt floor with its grey label sliding off the face, the man one stride from it, the cyan wake unbroken behind him.
beats.impact: The five clears are released in exactly the order the five problems arrived, so the second half of the film is the first half being answered rather than a new list. One tick on screen at a time, always the same lower-third zone, each held long enough to be read aloud at delivery size. No cut inside the beat; the events pass through the single travelling frame. The tone continues to rise without a level change, so nothing here reads as a jingle carrying the message.

beats.title: His own roof
beats.feeling: Standing higher than you started, in a place you own, with the month behind you - earned calm, not celebration.
beats.framing: The last flattened slab ramps up at its far end and he runs up it; the camera leaves the floor band for the only time and lifts with him in one continuous vertical move onto the roof of his own building. The vertical frame finally shows what the format was for: the black water tank on its welded steel frame at the top of the long axis, the whole cleared run of the level receding below at the bottom. He puts one hand on the tank frame and stops, turning to look back down the level. The phone hangs low in his other hand, screen inward, throwing cyan up onto his forearm and the underside of his jaw.
beats.first_frame: His leading foot on the up-ramp of the last slab, the roofline entering the top of the frame for the first time in the film, the water tank still cut by the upper frame edge.
beats.impact: The only vertical move in thirty seconds, motivated entirely by the climb, and the only moment the level is seen whole - the beat earns the 9:16 frame rather than inheriting it from the platform. No text composites anywhere in this beat: the frame has to sell on its own or it has not done its job. The rising tone resolves and the bed stops a second before the beat ends, leaving clean rooftop ambience under the hero frame so the last thing before the card is quiet.

beats.title: The card
beats.feeling: Settled. One thing to do, and it takes four words.
beats.framing: Code-composed, no generated picture at all: a flat cobalt #0038FF field; the supplied RentOK wordmark placed unaltered in the upper-centre zone, Rent in white and Ok in #03FFF1 on the cobalt ground, never redrawn, recoloured or regenerated; INSTALL and RENTOK APP composited beneath it as two lines; RENTOK.COM in the lower third, above a bottom margin kept clear of the platform's own interface overlays.
beats.first_frame: The cobalt field arriving as a single hard cut straight out of the rooftop - no dissolve, no wipe, no animation on the mark.
beats.impact: A hard cut and then a hold: three strings and one mark, held for the time it takes to read them aloud, which is what a still frame of this density needs. This is the only moment in the film where offer, benefit and action sit together, and it is the frame a muted scroller stops on, so it is built to be grunted back on its own with the sound off. The mark is the supplied file; on this cobalt ground the brand's own two-colour lockup is the variant used, never an author-chosen recolour.

obstacle_face_upper.why: The problems are what the top of the long axis is for: each label sits on the blank slab face, opposed across the vertical frame to the man on the cobalt band at the bottom, so the format itself states the relation between him and what is in front of him. One label on screen at a time, always in the same zone, each entering as its obstacle completes its arrival and leaving before the next. Set in a wide unrounded grotesque with thick strokes; the strings are short labels rather than running lines, so the all-capitals objection in does not reach them by its own scope, and each block is measured against the pixels of the grey slab beneath it for at least 4.5:1.

cheat_code_over_screen.why: The ask and the name arrive together on the one frame where the whole screen is the product, and RENTOK APP lands at 9.4 s, inside the ten seconds that attribution needs. Both lines sit over flat cyan #03FFF1 with the white weight and size fixed for at least 4.5:1 on that measured field; INSTALL leads and RENTOK APP follows beneath it, so the action is read before the name rather than after it.

feature_ticks_lower_third.why: Each tick answers one problem and is released in the same order the problems arrived, so the release order does the explaining and nothing has to be argued. They sit in the lower third, just above the cobalt band and diagonally opposite the zone the grey problem labels used, so the eye reads the swap as a swap. Cyan on graded-down grey, one at a time, each held for its read-aloud time at phone size.

close_card_ask.why: The ask repeats at the end, more direct than at its first appearance, under the mark and above the URL. This is the frame a muted viewer stops on, so it carries the action in plain words with no picture competing for the same attention.

close_card_url.why: The address is the last thing in and the smallest rank of three, placed in the lower third and kept above a bottom margin clear of the Reels and Shorts interface overlays, so it is still findable at delivery size on a phone.

mandatory.customer_words: I want to make a video for RentOK. The video has a Mario game. The player is basically a PG owner.
mandatory.realisation: The whole thirty seconds is a playable level and never breaks out of it: a single continuous left-to-right side-scrolling run with a HUD counter, a scrolling floor band, obstacles and a flag. The player character is the PG owner himself - one specific 52-year-old owner-operator, photographically rendered into the flat world, on screen in every beat except the code-composed close card.

mandatory.customer_words: The obstacles in the game are basically the problems that owner faces - tenant verification, collecting rent, tenants leaving without paying rent, no place to do reconciliation, solving complaints and so on.
mandatory.realisation: All five, in the customer's own order, each given a physical form that arrives at him rather than a caption: a slab for verification, a second slab for collecting rent, a tenant sprinting off frame with a mattress for leaving without paying, the floor folding open into a pit of loose paper slips for reconciliation, and cement chips raining off his own building for complaints. Beats 2 and 3 carry them.

mandatory.customer_words: The game also introduces a cheat code - install RentOK app.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4 is the cheat code and it is the film's hinge: the run stops dead, he enters it with his thumb on the real phone, the screen floods cyan and INSTALL and RENTOK APP composite over it before anything happens. It repeats more directly on the close card at beat 8.

mandatory.customer_words: Once it is done, Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity.
mandatory.realisation: The immunity mechanic is preserved exactly and the firearm is not: a thin cyan #03FFF1 outline snaps onto his silhouette at 13.0 s and stays for the rest of the film, with a cyan wake on the floor behind him. Nothing can stop him from that frame on - the pit closes under his foot, the slabs lie down, the falling debris stops in the air. Power-up design was delegated to the creative system by the brief; the mechanic requested was power and immunity, and immunity is what is built.

mandatory.customer_words: It runs and kills all the obstacles and gets the flag.
mandatory.realisation: All five obstacles are cleared on the run, in the order they were met, across beats 5 and 6 - not destroyed but laid flat into the floor so he runs across them. The flag is beat 7: the last flattened slab ramps up onto the roof of his own building and he takes hold of the steel frame of his own water tank.

mandatory.customer_words: Game identity: An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction of Nintendo's character, artwork, music or game assets.
mandatory.realisation: Nothing from that property appears: no plumber, no cap, no dungarees, no mushrooms, no coins, no question blocks, no turtles, no pixel font, no chiptune quotation. The level is built from this brand's own material instead - the cobalt floor band is the wordmark's own #0038FF, the power colour is the wordmark's own #03FFF1, the obstacles are cement slabs from this man's own building and the flagpole is his own water tank. The negative_line carries the exclusions into every prompt.
Exactly 30.0 s across eight contiguous beats, 0 to 30, with the eighth a code-composed card of clip_s 0.

mandatory.customer_words: Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts. aspect 9:16
mandatory.realisation: 9:16 throughout, and the format is justified by shape rather than by the platform alone: the film opposes two elements at the ends of the long axis - the man on the cobalt band at the bottom, the problem label on the slab face at the top - and pays the format off at beat 7, where a genuinely vertical subject, the water tank on its pole with the cleared level receding below, is the only thing that needed the tall frame. Text zones are kept clear of the platforms' own interface overlays, and the film is designed to survive muted autoplay.

mandatory.customer_words: subject: logo, rentok_wordmark; identity_invariants: Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1, blue #0038FF ground.
mandatory.realisation: All three invariants are load-bearing, not merely respected. #0038FF is the floor the entire level is built on, from frame one. #03FFF1 is the power itself and the only saturated colour in the film, set on the product in close-up at 8.8 s before it appears anywhere else. The white and cyan wordmark is placed from the supplied file, unaltered, at beat 4 and again on the close card.

All fifteen entries appear verbatim, including both duplicated INSTALL and RENTOK APP instances, as code-composited overlay plates in fixed zones with no reflow. Nothing legible is ever generated: every prompt specifies blank slab faces, blank screens, no signage and no lettering.

mandatory.customer_words: Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system.
mandatory.realisation: Declared and held: three tonal planes, two greys and one cobalt, a sparse frame of four objects, one light direction from upper frame-left, a photographically real man inside a flat world, and a single saturated hue that belongs to the product and to nothing else.

mandatory.customer_words: Power-up design: Delegated to the creative system, while preserving the requested game-style power/immunity mechanic.
mandatory.realisation: Declared: a cyan outline and floor wake rather than a weapon, and a clear that lays obstacles flat into the floor rather than destroying them - re-angled onto the product advantage, which is that the work does not disappear, it stops blocking him.

mandatory.customer_words: Brand and product source: Official RentOK website, https://rentok.com.
mandatory.realisation: The mark is the fetched site asset rentok_wordmark and no other; RENTOK.COM closes the film; and every feature string is flagged in copy_deck.sources for verification against rentok.com, plus an ASCI Code check, both outside Canon.

brand_timeline.in_context: The product is present from frame one - the phone is in his hand in the first shot and never leaves it - so the film never lapses, but the mark itself is held back until the cheat code so that the first frame can carry the surprise. From 9.4 s the brand is continuous in more than one asset type: the supplied wordmark on the screen at beat 4, then the brand's own #03FFF1 as the power that carries beats 5 to 7, the brand's own #0038FF as the floor under the entire film, the product in use in the hero frame, and the wordmark again on the closing card. The last frame is the mark.
brand_timeline.spoken: none. No voice of any kind is permitted, so the on-screen channel carries the name and the ask alone. This is a declared gap rather than a solved problem: the corpus states that its audio-and-super pairings assume sound is heard and does not say what replaces them on a sound-off feed.

last_frame: The close card held to 30.0 s: flat cobalt #0038FF, the supplied RentOK wordmark unaltered in the upper-centre zone with Rent in white and Ok in #03FFF1, INSTALL and RENTOK APP beneath it, RENTOK.COM in the lower third. The film ends on the mark.

deviations.from: / / default, ogx_0040: a commercial with a plethora of short scenes is below average at changing brand preference.
deviations.brief_clause: 'The obstacles in the game are basically the problems that owner faces - tenant verification, collecting rent, tenants leaving without paying rent, no place to do reconciliation, solving complaints and so on' together with 'Duration: 30 seconds' - five named obstacles and five named answers inside thirty seconds. Mitigated rather than ignored: the film is built as ONE continuous scene, a single lateral travel at constant speed into which the events arrive, with only two cuts off the axis in the whole thirty seconds, so what the source measured - a parade of separate scenes - is not what is built.

deviations.from: / default, ogx_0038 and ogx_0032 and mla_0064: cartoons are below average at selling to grown-ups, musical vignettes are impotent, and humour needs a brief clause and a writer who is one of the few.
deviations.brief_clause: 'The video has a Mario game' and 'Game identity: An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction of Nintendo's character, artwork, music or game assets.' The override is taken on the world only, not on the hero: the man is photographically real inside the flat world, because the evidence behind ogx_0038 is that live action holds where drawing does not. The film does not attempt jokes; the register is play, and nothing is staged at the owner's expense.

deviations.from: / / default, ogx_0042 and abcd_0021 and abcd_0012: supers say exactly the spoken words, the on-screen CTA is voiced in the same words, and the brand name is spoken as well as shown.
deviations.brief_clause: 'Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts' - sound-off autoplay feeds - and the job's standing production constraint of no dialogue or voice-over. 's own LIMIT records that the corpus does not say how the on-screen channel should carry ask and brand alone on such a feed, so this is declared as an uncovered case, not as a solved one; the film is built to pass muted and the audio is designed to be read as speech without containing any.

deviations.from: / / default, ogx_0009: specifics - a figure, a time, a sum - beat generalities, and every claim should be specific and traceable to a product fact.
deviations.brief_clause: 'exact_text_strings' is the customer's closed list of permitted on-screen words and contains no figure, and 'Brand and product source: Official RentOK website' supplies no verified number to this board. Inventing one would breach 's ban on an invented model number. The specificity is therefore paid in named sensory particulars instead - eleven at night, a hardbound paper register, loose reconciliation slips, a rolled mattress leaving the frame, five named capabilities - and no numeric claim is made anywhere.
